newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Petzetakis sees sales up in 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: Greek Petzetakis sees sales up in 1997-98.

text.p: Greek plastic pipe manufacturer Petzetakis' said on Friday sales are up 25 percent in the first five months of 1997.
Managers also told shareholders at its annual meeting turnover growth would stay high for through 1997 and 1998.
They based this forecast on a substantial rise in demand for rigid pipes used in sewerage, telecoms and natural gas projects in the Balkans and Middle East.
The enrichment of the product mix with high-tech flexible pipes for industrial use that are chanelled into the European Union (EU) market will also boost sales.
The company said it had adopted a strategy to produce custom-designed integrated pipe systems.
Consolidated pretax earnings in 1996 reached 507 million drachmas ($1.9 million) on turnover of 24.3 billion versus 33.2 billion and 316 million, respectively, in 1995.

Petzetakis completed a 3.9 billion restructuring plan to improve productivity, cut costs and relocate its flexible pipes production facilities to Thebes from Piraeus. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 272.7 Greek Drachmas)
